title: Instruction window / reorder buffer size selection under wire-delay constraint
where_in_paper: Introduction / front-end scheduling discussion, early pages
decision: Chose to keep the out-of-order issue window size moderate (the paper reports a 35-entry issue queue context / window around 35-40 instructions) rather to a much larger window
alternatives_or_rejected: Larger monolithic reorder/issue window; the paper argues against scaling window size much further because of wire delay across the die
rationale: Wire delay dominates at the target cycle time frequency; a larger centralized window would force the cycle to lengthen or operation to become multi-cycle, so the design accepted a smaller window to hit frequency
outcome: Achieves high frequency by keeping the window compact; paper presents this as the wire-delay-driven timing closure argument that shapes the floorplan
weakest_point: Exact window number (35 vs 40 vs 41) — I am uncertain whether the paper uses '35' or another figure; the qualitative argument about wire-delay limiting window size is the load-bearing point and I believe it is in the paper

title: Clustered integer execution units with inter-cluster communication
where_in_paper: Integer execution / instruction issue section, mid-article
decision: Split integer execution into two clusters (two sets of functional units) that each receive their own subset of instructions, with results forwarded between clusters via dedicated bypass paths
alternatives_or_rejected: Single unified integer cluster / monolithic execution datapath; the paper argues-delay / fan-in made a single cluster unattractive at the target cycle
rationale: Wire delay and register-file/queue port scaling at high frequency make a single central issue structure and unified RF impractical; clustering localizes wires and lets each half run fast
outcome: Paper reports two integer clusters with arbitration at issue and inter-cluster result forwarding; compiler/scheduler mitigates some imbalance
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly frames this as 'considered and rejected a unified cluster' vs. just describes the clustered design; the clustered design itself is definitely in the paper

title: Replicated instruction cache (dual I-cache ports / mirrored paths) to feed two clustered integer halves
where_in_paper / front-end section
decision: Replicated the instruction cache (or its output paths) so each cluster can be fed from its own copy/port, rather than broadcasting from one cache to two clusters over long
alternatives_or_rejected: Single shared I-cache feeding both clusters over long wires; rejected on wire-delay / cycle-time grounds
rationale: Wire delay from a single I-cache output to both clusters would not meet cycle time at the target frequency; replication shortens the wires and lets each side locally
outcome: Paper reports the replicated I-cache arrangement enabling the clustered integer pipeline to meet frequency targets
weakest_point: I am less certain this specific replication rationale is stated explicitly as a weighed decision; it may be presented more as a structural consequence than a debated choice

title: Wire-delay-driven floorplanning with timing-driven placement
where_in_paper: Physical design / floorplanning discussion, later pages
decision: Adopted a timing-driven / wire-delay-aware floorplan (with regional placement of pipeline latches and balanced wire budgets) rather than a purely functional or area-driven layout
alternatives_or_rejected: Functional floorplanning without explicit timing budgets; the paper argues this would not close timing at the target cycle
rationale: At the 21264's cycle time and process, wire delay rivals or exceeds gate delay; cycle time can only be met by floorplanning that budgets wire lengths and inserts pipeline latches along long paths
outcome: Paper presents the wire-delay-balanced floorplan (including the well-known quad/cluster placement) as the means of achieving the aggressive cycle
weakest_point: Whether this is framed as an explicit decision- with rejected alternatives vs. described as a methodology; qualitative argument is high confidence, exact phrasing uncertain

title: Frequency / IPC trade-off positioning
decision: Positioned the design toward maximizing clock frequency (with moderate issue width and modest window) rather than maximizing IPC at lower frequency
alternatives_or_rejected: Higher-IPC / lower-frequency design point; the paper argues this was explicitly considered
rationale: Paper's stated rationale: in the target performance envelope and with the given process, overall performance favored high frequency over deeper issue, and wire-delay constraints reinforced that choice
outcome: Paper reports the resulting frequency / SPEC performance numbers consistent with this trade-off
weakest_point: I am least certain as a weighed decision in this. being general P6/21264 industry commentary; weakest of the five entries
